Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.

43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.

standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)

view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),

common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis uses item embeddings and sequence-conditioned scores. `item_emb.weight` supplies item vectors; `log2feats(sequence)` computes per-position sequence representations; `predict_score(features, items)` scores positive and negative items at each position. The model implementation is absent, so the encoder architecture and exact representation computation cannot be verified. This probe evaluates all valid positions, rather than selecting a final user vector.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` receives the compatibility view and stores its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently consulted; stored reviews and histories are unused.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` processes up to ten batches of `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, with tensors shaped B × L. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; stacked positive/negative IDs pass to `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Scoring runs in evaluation mode without gradients; the previous training mode is not restored.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, and averages off-diagonal cosine similarities. Mapping via `(mean_cosine + 1)/2` produces the score. Higher values indicate directional alignment; roughly 0.5 corresponds to near-zero average similarity, not necessarily collapse.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits. Higher values indicate stronger separation, including among difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts positive/negative item categories separately for low-margin and incorrectly ranked positions, retaining the top twenty categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

There are no sequence perturbations, shuffling, ablations, or sensitivity tests. Random sampling only limits embedding analysis; negatives come from the loader.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The raw result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. A separate prompt requests an interpreted JSON summary containing status, findings, implications, and evidence; it does not itself execute interpretation.

These training-batch probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, generalization, or simulator traits. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists should be empty; counts cannot establish category-specific weaknesses. Mean cosine alone cannot establish representation diversity or rank.

Sampled ranking can change model ordering, rather than merely rescale accuracy: RecSys 2025’s [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) reports sampling-dependent evaluation bias. A [2024 reproduction study](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989) also identifies evaluation strategy and user grouping as factors behind inconsistent popularity-bias findings. Practical implication: retain pinned sampled HR@10 for selection; separately measure sampled/full-catalog hit disagreement and model-order agreement on a fixed, bounded user panel. Stratify failures by target-item training frequency and user history length; report stratum sizes. Full-catalog evaluation still has incomplete relevance labels.

Embedding spectrum offers a more informative collapse diagnostic than mean cosine. [Guo et al., ICML 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) document recommendation embedding collapse and interactions that constrain embedding dimensionality. Proposed probe: exclude padding, fix item sampling and centering conventions, compute normalized effective rank exp(−Σpᵢlog pᵢ), with pᵢ proportional to singular values; accompany it with leading-component mass and embedding norms. These describe geometry, not guaranteed recommendation quality.

Controlled-fault validation remains a proposed experiment; the retrieved evidence does not establish a probe that predicts improvements across these four datasets. shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis uses item embeddings and sequence-conditioned scores. `item_emb.weight` supplies item vectors; `log2feats(sequence)` computes per-position sequence representations; `predict_score(features, items)` scores positive and negative items at each position. The model implementation is absent, so the encoder architecture and exact representation computation cannot be verified. This probe evaluates all valid positions, rather than selecting a final user vector.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` receives the compatibility view and stores its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently consulted; stored reviews and histories are unused.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` processes up to ten batches of `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, with tensors shaped B × L. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; stacked positive/negative IDs pass to `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Scoring runs in evaluation mode without gradients; the previous training mode is not restored.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, and averages off-diagonal cosine similarities. Mapping via `(mean_cosine + 1)/2` produces the score. Higher values indicate directional alignment; roughly 0.5 corresponds to near-zero average similarity, not necessarily collapse.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits. Higher values indicate stronger separation, including among difficult positions.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts positive/negative item categories separately for low-margin and incorrectly ranked positions, retaining the top twenty categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

There are no sequence perturbations, shuffling, ablations, or sensitivity tests. Random sampling only limits embedding analysis; negatives come from the loader.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The raw result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. A separate prompt requests an interpreted JSON summary containing status, findings, implications, and evidence; it does not itself execute interpretation.

These training-batch probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, generalization, or simulator traits. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists should be empty; counts cannot establish category-specific weaknesses. Mean cosine alone cannot establish representation diversity or rank.
